title: Transcode status poller and its tests
name: Transcode status poller

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in these tests that could make any of them pass on some runs and fail on others? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: There is none. The poller is time-based, but the tests never depend on real time: the Sleeper is injected, and RecordingSleeper resolves immediately while recording the requested delays. ScriptedTranscoder returns a fixed sequence of states, so the number of polls is deterministic. The order in which the API returns renditions doesn't matter, because waitForRenditions sorts a copy before returning and the test expects the sorted array. Each test builds its own fakes, so no state leaks between tests.

choiceQuestions.prompt: With maxPolls 4 and a job that never leaves "transcoding", how long does waitForRenditions spend sleeping in production (realSleeper, intervalMs 2000)?
choices: 0 seconds; it throws on the first poll
choiceQuestions.explanation: It sleeps after polls 1, 2 and 3 but skips the sleep after the 4th because attempt < maxPolls is false, then throws TranscodeTimeoutError. That is 3 x 2000 ms = 6 s. 8 s would need a sleep after the last poll, and 2 s and 0 s ignore the loop.

choiceQuestions.prompt: ScriptedTranscoder is given the script ["transcoding"] and polled 4 times. What state does it return on the 4th call?
choices: undefined, because the index is past the end of the script
"transcoding", because the index is clamped to the last script entry
choiceQuestions.explanation: getStatus uses Math.min(this.calls, this.script.length - 1), so once the script runs out it keeps returning the last entry. Nothing in the fake returns undefined, defaults to "queued", or throws.

choiceQuestions.prompt: What is the main benefit of passing a Sleeper into waitForRenditions instead of calling setTimeout directly?
choices: It lets the tests run instantly and assert on the exact delays requested, with no dependence on wall-clock timing
It makes production polling more accurate than setTimeout
It allows several jobs to be polled in parallel
It lets the caller cancel a poll in progress
choiceQuestions.explanation: With an injected Sleeper, the tests use RecordingSleeper, which returns immediately and records each ms value, so they are fast and deterministic. realSleeper is just setTimeout, so production accuracy is unchanged. This interface provides neither parallel polling nor cancellation.
